explanation_en: This idiomatic expression literally refers to a vehicle's reverse gear ('marcha atrás'), but metaphorically means that a decision or process is irreversible. It is widely used in both everyday conversation and formal news to describe situations that have reached a point of no return. It is a great alternative to saying 'es irreversible.'

examples.en_text: Once you sign the employment contract, there is no turning back.
examples.target_text: Una vez que firmes el contrato de trabajo, ya no hay marcha atrás.

examples.en_text: We have decided to sell the house and move to another city; there is no turning back now.
examples.target_text: Hemos decidido vender la casa y mudarnos a otra ciudad; ya no hay marcha atrás.

examples.en_text: Technology keeps advancing and there is no turning back in this process.
examples.target_text: La tecnología sigue avanzando y en este proceso no hay marcha atrás.

examples.en_text: I already told my boss that I am going to resign, so there is no turning back.
examples.target_text: Ya le dije a mi jefe que voy a renunciar, así que no hay marcha atrás.

examples.en_text: The plane is already taking off, now there really is no turning back.
examples.target_text: El avión ya está despegando, ahora sí que no hay marcha atrás.

examples.en_text: If you get that tattoo, remember that there is no turning back.
examples.target_text: Si te haces ese tatuaje, recuerda que no hay marcha atrás.

explanation_en: This metaphorical idiom is used to describe grouping different entities, concepts, or brands under a single unifying organization or category. It is highly common in business, corporate, and political Spanish. It is a direct equivalent of the English 'under the same umbrella' and is highly idiomatic in both languages.

examples.en_text: All of these clothing brands belong to the same company and operate under the same umbrella.
examples.target_text: Todas estas marcas de ropa pertenecen a la misma empresa y operan bajo el mismo paraguas.

examples.en_text: The government decided to unite the environmental projects under the same umbrella to save resources.
examples.target_text: El gobierno decidió unir los proyectos de medio ambiente bajo el mismo paraguas para ahorrar recursos.

examples.en_text: Although we research different topics, we all work under the same umbrella in this department.
examples.target_text: Aunque investigamos temas diferentes, todos trabajamos bajo el mismo paraguas en este departamento.

examples.en_text: It started raining suddenly, so we had to walk under the same umbrella.
examples.target_text: Empezó a llover de repente, así que tuvimos que caminar bajo el mismo paraguas.

examples.en_text: The local clubs are now organized under the same umbrella of the national federation.
examples.target_text: Los clubes locales ahora están organizados bajo el mismo paraguas de la federación nacional.

examples.en_text: The company offers music, movies, and books, all under the same umbrella of its monthly subscription.
examples.target_text: La compañía ofrece música, películas y libros, todo bajo el mismo paraguas de su suscripción mensual.

explanation_en: Literally meaning 'elbow to elbow,' this expression is used to describe working closely and collaboratively with someone towards a common goal. It is highly common in professional, community, and emergency contexts. It functions as an adverbial phrase and does not change for gender or number.

examples.en_text: We worked side by side to finish the project on time.
examples.target_text: Trabajamos codo con codo para terminar el proyecto a tiempo.

examples.en_text: The neighbors cleaned the street side by side after the storm.
examples.target_text: Los vecinos limpiaron la calle codo con codo después de la tormenta.

examples.en_text: The two athletes ran side by side until they reached the finish line.
examples.target_text: Los dos atletas corrieron codo con codo hasta llegar a la meta.

examples.en_text: My brother and I run the family business side by side.
examples.target_text: Mi hermano y yo llevamos el negocio familiar codo con codo.

examples.en_text: Doctors and nurses fight side by side in the hospitals.
examples.target_text: Los médicos y los enfermeros luchan codo con codo en los hospitales.

examples.en_text: We have always overcome problems by working side by side.
examples.target_text: Siempre hemos superado los problemas trabajando codo con codo.

explanation_en: This expression means to break a temporary peace, pause, or respite. While it has literal military origins, it is frequently used metaphorically in news and daily life to describe a sudden disruption of a calm period, such as a resurgence of bad weather, illness, or, in this case, wildfires.

examples.en_text: My brother always breaks the truce when we start talking about politics.
examples.target_text: Mi hermano siempre rompe la tregua cuando empezamos a hablar de política.

examples.en_text: The rebel group broke the truce and attacked the city during the night.
examples.target_text: El grupo rebelde rompió la tregua y atacó la ciudad durante la noche.

examples.en_text: If the company reduces salaries, the union will break the truce and go back on strike.
examples.target_text: Si la empresa reduce los salarios, el sindicato romperá la tregua y volverá a la huelga.

examples.en_text: I don't want anyone to break the truce that was so hard for us to achieve in the office.
examples.target_text: No quiero que nadie rompa la tregua que tanto nos costó conseguir en la oficina.

examples.en_text: After months of peace, the sports press has broken the truce with the team's coach.
examples.target_text: Después de meses de paz, la prensa deportiva ha roto la tregua con el entrenador del equipo.

examples.en_text: It's better not to say anything so as not to break the family truce during Christmas dinner.
examples.target_text: Es mejor no decir nada para no romper la tregua familiar durante la cena de Navidad.

explanation_en: The idiom 'dar un respiro' means to provide a temporary relief, break, or pause from a stressful or intense situation. It is widely used in both formal news reporting and informal conversations when talking about work, weather, or difficult tasks. Note that the recipient of the 'respiro' is typically introduced with an indirect object pronoun (e.g., 'nos dio un respiro').

examples.en_text: The drop in temperatures has given us a break after a week of extreme heat.
examples.target_text: La bajada de las temperaturas nos ha dado un respiro después de una semana de calor extremo.

examples.en_text: Work has finally given me a break and this weekend I'm not going to turn on the computer.
examples.target_text: El trabajo por fin me ha dado un respiro y este fin de semana no voy a encender el ordenador.

examples.en_text: Fortunately, the cough has given the girl a break and she was able to sleep all night.
examples.target_text: Afortunadamente, la tos le ha dado un respiro a la niña y ha podido dormir toda la noche.

examples.en_text: The bank has given us a break this month by postponing the mortgage payment.
examples.target_text: El banco nos ha dado un respiro este mes al aplazar el pago de la hipoteca.

examples.en_text: The press hasn't given the president a break after the latest scandal.
examples.target_text: La prensa no le ha dado un respiro al presidente tras el último escándalo.

examples.en_text: My old car has given me a break and didn't break down during the trip.
examples.target_text: Mi viejo coche me ha dado un respiro y no se ha estropeado durante el viaje.

explanation_en: This phrase means to shift from a defensive posture to an active, aggressive approach to solve a problem. It is a common journalistic and sports metaphor used when a group stops merely reacting to a threat and begins actively combating it. It is always used with the preposition 'a'.

examples.en_text: After seeing the competition's new strategy, the company decided to go on the offensive.
examples.target_text: Tras ver la nueva estrategia de la competencia, la empresa decidió pasar a la ofensiva.

examples.en_text: The team was losing, but in the second half they have gone on the offensive.
examples.target_text: El equipo iba perdiendo, pero en la segunda parte ha pasado a la ofensiva.

examples.en_text: If they keep criticizing you, you should go on the offensive and defend your ideas.
examples.target_text: Si siguen criticándote, deberías pasar a la ofensiva y defender tus ideas.

examples.en_text: The candidate went on the offensive during the debate to win more votes.
examples.target_text: El candidato pasó a la ofensiva durante el debate para ganar más votos.

examples.en_text: Instead of apologizing, he is going on the offensive to blame others.
examples.target_text: En lugar de disculparse, él está pasando a la ofensiva para culpar a los demás.

examples.en_text: We cannot keep waiting; tomorrow we will go on the offensive to solve this problem.
examples.target_text: No podemos seguir esperando; mañana pasaremos a la ofensiva para resolver este problema.

explanation_en: The pronominal verb 'volcarse' (literally 'to tip over') means to devote oneself entirely to a cause, person, or task with great enthusiasm and effort. It is a very common B2/C1 level verb used to describe community solidarity or personal dedication. It is typically followed by the prepositions 'con' or 'en' (e.g., 'se volcaron con los afectados').

examples.en_text: The neighbors have gone all out to help the family who lost their home in the fire.
examples.target_text: Los vecinos se han volcado para ayudar a la familia que perdió su casa en el incendio.

examples.en_text: My parents have gone all out with my new project and have supported me from the beginning.
examples.target_text: Mis padres se han volcado con mi nuevo proyecto y me han apoyado desde el principio.

examples.en_text: The volunteers have gone all out in organizing this year's charity festival.
examples.target_text: Los voluntarios se han volcado en la organización del festival benéfico de este año.

examples.en_text: In this hotel, they have gone all out to make our stay perfect.
examples.target_text: En este hotel se han volcado para que nuestra estancia fuera perfecta.

examples.en_text: The fans have gone all out for the football team after last week's defeat.
examples.target_text: Los aficionados se han volcado con el equipo de fútbol tras la derrota de la semana pasada.

examples.en_text: The teachers have gone all out to adapt the classes to the needs of each student.
examples.target_text: Los profesores se han volcado para adaptar las clases a las necesidades de cada alumno.

explanation_en: Derived from the chess term 'check' (jaque), 'mantener en jaque' means to keep someone or something in a state of constant threat, danger, or alert. It is a highly sophisticated yet common journalistic expression used to describe situations where an adversary, disease, or natural disaster poses an ongoing challenge.

examples.en_text: The snowstorm has kept the entire city on edge over the weekend.
examples.target_text: La tormenta de nieve ha mantenido en jaque a toda la ciudad durante el fin de semana.

examples.en_text: This new virus has kept doctors across the country on edge.
examples.target_text: Este nuevo virus ha mantenido en jaque a los médicos de todo el país.

examples.en_text: Constant inflation has kept small businesses on edge this year.
examples.target_text: La inflación constante ha mantenido en jaque a las pequeñas empresas este año.

examples.en_text: The clever thief has kept the local police on edge for months.
examples.target_text: El astuto ladrón ha mantenido en jaque a la policía local por meses.

examples.en_text: The cyberattack has kept the banking system on edge for hours.
examples.target_text: El ataque informático ha mantenido en jaque al sistema bancario durante horas.

examples.en_text: The rival team has kept us on edge during the entire second half of the match.
examples.target_text: El equipo rival nos ha mantenido en jaque durante toda la segunda parte del partido.

idiom: en cuanto a violencia machista se refiere
explanation_en: This is a highly useful B2/C1 formulaic frame: 'en cuanto a [noun] se refiere' (as far as [noun] is concerned). It is more sophisticated than simply using 'sobre' or 'en cuanto a' alone. Note that the verb 'referirse' remains in the singular 'se refiere' because it functions as an impersonal construction, regardless of whether the preceding noun is singular or plural.

examples.en_text: The government has launched a new education campaign, especially as far as gender-based violence is concerned.
examples.target_text: El gobierno ha lanzado una nueva campaña de educación, especialmente en cuanto a violencia machista se refiere.

examples.en_text: There is still a lot left to do in our country as far as gender-based violence is concerned.
examples.target_text: Todavía queda mucho por hacer en nuestro país en cuanto a violencia machista se refiere.

examples.en_text: Statistics show a slight improvement this year as far as gender-based violence is concerned.
examples.target_text: Las estadísticas muestran una leve mejoría este año en cuanto a violencia machista se refiere.

examples.en_text: The media has a great responsibility as far as gender-based violence is concerned.
examples.target_text: Los medios de comunicación tienen una gran responsabilidad en cuanto a violencia machista se refiere.

examples.en_text: It is essential to offer free psychological support as far as gender-based violence is concerned.
examples.target_text: Es fundamental ofrecer apoyo psicológico gratuito en cuanto a violencia machista se refiere.

examples.en_text: We cannot lower our guard as far as gender-based violence is concerned; we must continue educating young people.
examples.target_text: No podemos bajar la guardia en cuanto a violencia machista se refiere, debemos seguir educando a los jóvenes.

explanation_en: An idiomatic binomial pair equivalent to 'loud and clear'. Note that 'alto' functions as an adverb here meaning 'loudly' (not 'tall'), so it does not change to agree with the speaker or subject. It is widely used in both political speeches and everyday arguments to express absolute certainty and assertiveness.

examples.en_text: Can you hear me well at the back of the room? Yes, I hear you loud and clear.
examples.target_text: ¿Me escuchas bien al fondo de la sala? Sí, te oigo alto y claro.

examples.en_text: The director made it loud and clear that no delays on the project will be allowed.
examples.target_text: El director dejó alto y claro que no se permitirán retrasos en el proyecto.

examples.en_text: The radio signal is excellent; the message is received loud and clear.
examples.target_text: La señal de radio es excelente; el mensaje se recibe alto y claro.

examples.en_text: I want you to tell me loud and clear if you agree with this decision.
examples.target_text: Quiero que me digas alto y claro si estás de acuerdo con esta decisión.

examples.en_text: The protesters spoke loud and clear to defend their rights.
examples.target_text: Los manifestantes hablaron alto y claro para defender sus derechos.

examples.en_text: Please repeat the answer loud and clear so that the whole class can hear you.
examples.target_text: Por favor, repite la respuesta alto y claro para que toda la clase pueda oírte.

explanation_en: Derived from 'paliativo' (palliative/mitigating), the phrase 'sin paliativos' means absolute, outright, or without any excuses or softening. It is a high-register collocation frequently found in editorials, political discourse, and formal debates to describe a stance, defeat, or condemnation that is total and unconditional.

examples.en_text: The project was an unmitigated failure; we lost all the invested money.
examples.target_text: El proyecto fue un fracaso sin paliativos; perdimos todo el dinero invertido.

examples.en_text: The government expressed its outright rejection of the violence in the streets.
examples.target_text: El gobierno expresó su rechazo sin paliativos a la violencia en las calles.

examples.en_text: If we want to solve the problem, we must speak with sincerity and without half measures.
examples.target_text: Si queremos solucionar el problema, debemos hablar con sinceridad y sin paliativos.

examples.en_text: The team achieved an absolute victory in the last game of the season.
examples.target_text: El equipo consiguió una victoria sin paliativos en el último partido de la temporada.

examples.en_text: I demand an outright apology for the behavior you showed yesterday.
examples.target_text: Exijo una disculpa sin paliativos por el comportamiento que tuviste ayer.

examples.en_text: My parents gave me their unconditional support when I decided to change my major.
examples.target_text: Mis padres me dieron su apoyo sin paliativos cuando decidí cambiar de carrera.

explanation_en: An idiomatic expression meaning to deliberately ignore a problem, turn a blind eye, or avoid taking responsibility. It can be used with the prepositions 'hacia' or 'a' (e.g., 'mirar a otro lado'). It is a powerful figurative phrase common in social, political, and moral contexts.

examples.en_text: The government cannot look the other way in the face of this serious social problem.
examples.target_text: El gobierno no puede mirar hacia otro lado ante este grave problema social.

examples.en_text: When they gave me the vaccine, I preferred to look the other way so as not to see the needle.
examples.target_text: Cuando me pusieron la vacuna, preferí mirar hacia otro lado para no ver la aguja.

examples.en_text: If you see someone being bullied at school, you shouldn't look the other way.
examples.target_text: Si ves que alguien sufre acoso en la escuela, no debes mirar hacia otro lado.

examples.en_text: The boss knew there were errors in the accounts, but he decided to look the other way.
examples.target_text: El jefe sabía que había errores en las cuentas, pero decidió mirar hacia otro lado.

examples.en_text: Why did you look the other way when I waved at you on the street yesterday?
examples.target_text: ¿Por qué miraste hacia otro lado cuando te saludé en la calle ayer?

examples.en_text: We cannot keep looking the other way in the face of the climate change crisis.
examples.target_text: No podemos seguir mirando hacia otro lado ante la crisis del cambio climático.
